# Resolve Free

`voyager resolve free-import` (Resolve 18.5 or later) puts a cut into Resolve and
`voyager resolve free-edit` (Resolve 21.1 or later) adds titles, Fusion motion
graphics with keyframes, transitions, fades, framing, prepared audio mixes, clip audio level,
CDL and LUT grades, clip color labels, speed, markers, captions from an SRT
and a render with them burned in.

If the user has DaVinci Resolve Studio, record it with `voyager resolve edition --set
studio`; Voyager uses [the Studio workflow](studio-resolve.md) from their next chat.

## Read-only for the user's work

Every free command reaches Resolve through one Voyager-owned Workspace > Scripts
entry: a file in Resolve's Scripts folder that Voyager installs once (usually when it
detects Resolve) and rewrites per job. Results come back as interchange files in
Voyager's own state folder, written through a temporary UI layout preset that is
deleted at once. These are not renders. `free-inspect`, and `free-edit` with
`"operations": []`, no `render` and the open project's name, never change the user's
project, timelines, settings or media; naming another project makes Resolve open it.
Only `free-import` (a new timeline in a Voyager project) and an edit with operations or
a render change anything in Resolve.

So a request to look without changing anything fits them: say what they write (Voyager's
own script file and files in its own folder, nothing in the project) and run them. If
the user has ruled out even that, for example no new files at all, ask before running.

To see what is open, run:

```sh
voyager resolve free-inspect --json
```

It returns the open project's name, its timeline and media pool item counts, and the
open timeline's name, fps and length in frames (`timeline` is null when none is open),
without loading another project or exporting a timeline. It never starts Resolve
(`RESOLVE_NOT_RUNNING`) and needs a project open (`NO_PROJECT`). For that
timeline's clips, titles and markers, pass the returned `project` to the empty
`free-edit` below.

## What Voyager can do in free Resolve today

**Cannot yet:** lift/gamma/gain wheels, curves, qualifiers, windows or new color
nodes, speed ramps, Edit-page OpenFX effects, or caption background, font and
position controls.
Voyager's free-edition commands do not reach these yet.

Existing-title text edits, A/V linking, project close/reopen cycles and DRP export are
outside `free-import`/`free-edit`/`free-inspect`; QA required custom in-app Lua.
`title` adds a new title.

Describe only what `free-import`, `free-edit` and `free-inspect` do as things you can do. When the user asks for
something on the Cannot list, say it is not available in free Resolve through Voyager
yet, and offer what works: a new cut, media prepared with the existing media
tools before import (baked in, so not editable in Resolve), or a finished video
rendered with Voyager's own tools outside Resolve.
Motion graphics, animated or styled titles and keyframed moves are built natively
in Resolve's Fusion with the `motion` operation below, editable on the Fusion page;
a plain lower third is a `title`. Render a graphic outside Resolve and import it only
when the user prefers that (HyperFrames `render --format mov` is ProRes 4444 with
alpha; place the `.mov` on video track 2 of a new cut with `free-import`, and its
text is not editable there). Never re-import a timeline that is already in Resolve
to add to it. Use an `audio` operation to add a prepared sound mix to an existing
cut, preserving its in-Resolve edits.

Edit a timeline Voyager put in Resolve with one command:

```sh
voyager resolve free-edit --input @edit.json --json
```

```json
{
  "project": "Voyager Cut v1",
  "timeline": "Cut v1 (2026-09-23 10.00.00)",
  "operations": [
    { "op": "title", "text": "Launch day", "at": 0, "frames": 48 },
    { "op": "transition", "clip": 2, "frames": 12 },
    { "op": "fade", "edge": "out", "frames": 24 },
    { "op": "fade", "edge": "out", "kind": "audio", "frames": 24 },
    { "op": "transform", "clip": 1, "zoom": 1.2 },
    { "op": "volume", "clip": 2, "db": -6 },
    { "op": "audio", "file": "audio/mix.wav", "at": 0, "track": "new", "db": -6 },
    { "op": "cdl", "clip": 1, "slope": [1.1, 1, 0.95], "offset": [0, 0, 0], "power": [1, 1, 1], "saturation": 0.9 },
    { "op": "speed", "clip": 2, "percentage": 50 },
    { "op": "marker", "at": 48, "color": "Blue", "name": "Review", "note": "Check the grade" },
    { "op": "captions", "srt": "speech/captions.srt" }
  ],
  "render": "exports/launch.mp4"
}
```

Leave out `timeline` to edit the one open in Resolve. The user may have changed it since
your last edit: before placing anything by position, run the edit with `"operations": []`.
That changes nothing and returns the project's timelines and the timeline's clips (numbered
as `clip` takes them, each with its `start` and `frames` on the timeline and, for media, the
`sourceIn` frame it starts on at its `sourceFps`, counted from the file's first frame as an
import's `start` is), title texts and markers. Frames count from the timeline start, at the
result's `fps`: the rate the timeline plays and renders at, from its settings (the project's
when it uses project settings). Use that `fps` for a new cut of this project; `otioFps` and a
warning appear when Resolve's export labels the timeline with another, stored rate. Speed operations
run first, whatever their place in the list, so every position in the edit (a
title's `at`, an audio mix's `at`, a marker's `at`, caption cue times) is a frame on the timeline after
its speed changes: a rippled speed change moves the clips after it, so place titles,
markers and captions against the retimed cut, not the imported one. `clip` is the
clip's 1-based position on its track (default track 1; `kind: "audio"` for audio);
a transition goes on the later of two clips and needs source frames beyond the
cut, so trim clips short of their source ends. Operations: `title` (text, `at`,
`frames`, optional `x` and `y` for its centre, 0-1 from the bottom left, and `size`), `transition` (`clip`, `frames`), `fade` (`edge` in or out, `frames`,
optional `clip`), `transform` (`clip` and any of `zoom`, `pan`, `tilt`,
`rotation`, `cropLeft`, `cropRight`, `cropTop`, `cropBottom`), `volume` (`clip`,
`db`; always an audio clip, so `kind: "audio"` is optional), `cdl` (`clip`, three-number `slope`, `offset` and `power`, `saturation`,
optional `node`), `lut` (`clip`, `path` absolute or relative to Resolve's LUT
folder, optional `node`), `clipColor` (`clip`, a Resolve clip color such as
`Blue` or `Orange`), `speed` (`clip`, `percentage`; `ripple: true` moves the clips
after it, the default keeps them in place; a fade or transition on a retimed clip keeps its requested length), `marker` (`at`, a Resolve marker
color, `name`, optional `note` and `frames`), `captions` (`srt`, an .srt path; once
per edit; optional `replace: true` replaces one existing subtitle track on the
new edit version, while the source stays unchanged; multiple subtitle tracks are
refused). Without `replace`, existing subtitles are refused. Each cue lands at its SRT time
counted from the timeline start, so edit-video's speech-edit `captions.srt`, timed from its
`speech.wav`, fits a timeline where that audio starts at frame 0.

`audio` takes an audio-only `file` and `at` (frames from the timeline start).
Omit `track` or use `"new"` for its own new audio track; a numeric `track` selects an
existing 1-based audio track. A new track preserves the file's channel count (mono,
stereo or adaptive for more channels); an existing track with fewer channels is
refused. Optional `sourceIn` counts frames from the file's first
frame at the imported media's `sourceFps`; optional `frames` is the length at the
timeline's `fps` (otherwise the remaining source is used). `sourceIn` defaults to
zero. Optional `db` sets the
clip's audio volume, -100 to 30 dB. An overlap is refused unless `replace: true`,
which removes the whole overlapping audio clips on that track from the new edit
version, without ripple. The source timeline stays unchanged. Clip selectors for
other operations refer to the clips present before the edit; use `audio`'s `db` for
the new mix and inspect the returned version before addressing its clips.
The operation reports its `itemId`, track, position and length. A misplaced mix,
changed video track or missing save fails the operation; a mismatch in the exported
audio readback makes the edit `partial` and lists the problem.

`node` is an existing 1-based color node (default 1); Voyager cannot add nodes. A CDL is Resolve's slope/offset/power,
not lift/gamma/gain, and Resolve cannot read one back: the result lists it under
`unverified`, so say the grade was set but check it on the Color page or in a
render before calling it right. `render` is a new .mp4 or .mov path; nothing is overwritten, it renders
only when every operation succeeded, and captions added in the same edit are
burned into the picture. The edit lands
on a new timeline version and the one it started from is unchanged. If any
operation fails, nothing is kept: the version is removed and the result
(`OPERATION_FAILED`) names each failed operation, so fix it and run the whole edit
again. Editing a version names the new one after the original timeline, not after
the version. A
transition or fade whose length in Resolve differs from what it reported makes the
edit `partial`, as does a timeline marker that moved.

A title or a new composition clip goes on a new top video track with every other track,
subtitles included, locked; timeline markers it shifted are put back where they were. If
an item on another track moved, the timeline grew past the new clip's end, or a marker
could not be put back, that operation fails with `RIPPLED`: say so rather than retrying
the same edit.

Observed on Free 21.1.1.10: incoming one-frame audio fades failed after preceding outgoing
fades at shared contiguous seams (`FADE_FAILED`). Retry without conflicting incoming fades.

Render checks stable nonzero size and matching probed video-frame count; reports
audio-stream presence. No decoding or picture/audio/caption verification.

### Motion graphics in Fusion

`motion` builds a Fusion node graph from data: tools, their input values, keyframes
and connections. With `at` and `frames` it adds a Fusion composition clip on a new
top video track, composited over the footage (a lower third, an animated title, a
shape reveal). With `clip` (and optional `track`) it builds the clip's own
composition, fed by its `MediaIn`, for a keyframed push-in, a blur or a glow on
the footage; a clip that already has a Fusion composition is refused.

```json
{
  "op": "motion", "at": 24, "frames": 72,
  "tools": [
    { "name": "Title", "type": "TextPlus", "inputs": { "StyledText": "Launch day", "Font": "Open Sans", "Style": "Bold", "Size": 0.09, "Red1": 1, "Green1": 0.85, "Blue1": 0.2 },
      "keyframes": { "Center": [{ "frame": 0, "value": [0.5, -0.1] }, { "frame": 12, "value": [0.5, 0.2] }] } },
    { "name": "Grow", "type": "Transform", "keyframes": { "Size": [{ "frame": 0, "value": 0.8 }, { "frame": 12, "value": 1 }] } }
  ],
  "connections": [{ "to": "Grow", "input": "Input", "from": "Title" }],
  "output": "Grow"
}
```

```json
{
  "op": "motion", "clip": 1,
  "tools": [{ "name": "Push", "type": "Transform", "keyframes": { "Size": [{ "frame": 0, "value": 1 }, { "frame": 96, "value": 1.15 }] } }],
  "connections": [{ "to": "Push", "input": "Input", "from": "MediaIn" }],
  "output": "Push"
}
```

`type` is a Fusion tool ID (`TextPlus`, `Background`, `Merge`, `Transform`,
`RectangleMask`, `EllipseMask`, `Blur`, `Glow`, `ColorCorrector`, `FastNoise`,
`sRectangle`, `sEllipse`, `sRender`, ...; Resize is `Resize` or its ID `BetterResize`); `name` is how connections and results refer to it and
becomes the node's name. `inputs` and `keyframes` use Fusion input IDs as Fusion's
scripting names them (`Center`, `Size`, `Angle`, `Blend`, `StyledText`, `Font`,
`Red1`, `Merge` `Background`/`Foreground`/`Center`/`Size`, a mask's `Width`,
`Height`). Values are numbers, strings, or `[x, y]` points in 0..1 of the frame.
Keyframe `frame` counts from the clip's first frame (0) and must fall inside it;
an input is either set or keyframed, not both. `connections` wire `from` a tool's
output into `to`'s `input`, and `output` feeds MediaOut. On a clip, `output` must
descend from `MediaIn`. A `type` outside the built-in drawing, compositing,
transform, mask and filter tools (no Loader, Saver, Custom tool or Fuse) is refused
with the list of available types, and so are render-script inputs. Inputs are set
in the order given, so put `Font` before `Style`.

Every value and keyframe is read back in Resolve, and a tool, input or connection
Resolve refuses fails the operation with its name (`NO_TOOL_<type>`,
`NO_INPUT_<tool>_<input>`, `INPUT_NOT_SET_...`, `KEYFRAME_NOT_SET_...`,
`NOT_CONNECTED_...`). A readback is not a render: check the result in a frame of
the render, or on the Fusion page, before calling a look right.

Put a cut into Resolve with one command:

```sh
voyager resolve free-import --input @cut.json --json
```

It writes the editable OTIO, then has Resolve import it through Voyager's
Workspace > Scripts > Voyager Import entry: into a dedicated Voyager project, one
per conversation, on a new timeline named with
the time, with source media linked. It starts Resolve in the background when it
is not running and leaves it on the Edit page. Its result is the verification:
Resolve's own export of the imported timeline, checked against the cut (clip and
frame counts, media file paths, offline items), plus the project Resolve left.
`linked` counts A/V timeline items with a nonempty media-pool `File Path`, not linked
A/V pairs. Report that result; do not screenshot Resolve or use computer control to confirm the
import. Each run adds a timeline; nothing is overwritten. Pass
`--project NAME` only when the user names a project, and `--switch-project` only after the
user agreed to leave the open project a `PROJECT_OPEN` refusal names. This is a scoped integration
step, not computer control: it needs no computer-use grant, but it needs macOS
Accessibility permission for Voyager. Under an agent sandbox, read Sandboxed agents below
first. To keep the
interchange file in the project, add `--path cut.otio`; `voyager resolve timeline
write --input @cut.json --path cut.otio` writes it without importing.
The cut list contains `name`, `fps`, and `clips`:

```json
{
  "name": "Cut v1",
  "fps": 24,
  "clips": [
    { "path": "shot.mp4", "start": 0, "end": 48, "at": 0, "track": 1, "kind": "video" },
    { "path": "voice.wav", "start": 0, "end": 48, "at": 0, "track": 1, "kind": "audio" }
  ]
}
```

Source ranges are end-exclusive frames at `sourceFps` (defaults to timeline fps),
counted from the file's first frame; `at` is timeline frames. Voyager adds a
source's embedded start timecode (camera clips, broadcast WAVs) itself, so never
add it to `start` or `end`. Paths resolve against the command's working directory.
A clip at another frame rate lasts `floor((end - start) * fps / sourceFps)` timeline frames (73 frames at 24 into 29.97 is 91), so place the next clip from that; the result's `conformed` lists each rounded clip with its `deltaFrames`. A cut whose `fps` differs from the rate Resolve plays the imported timeline at gets a warning and `timelineFps`. Use separate tracks for overlapping clips. A project Voyager creates takes the first
video clip's resolution and the cut's fps. An existing project keeps its own resolution and fps;
pass `--resolution 1920x1080` to set the resolution of a project that has no timelines yet. The
result's `projectSettings` is what the project uses, and `resolutionApplied` says whether this
import set it. This cut-only interchange does not apply effects, transitions or retiming.

## Sandboxed agents

`free-import`, `free-edit`, `free-inspect` and `edition --check` write outside the workspace and
reach macOS services that agent sandboxes deny, so run them outside the sandbox
from the start:

- **Codex:** run these commands with escalated permissions (outside the sandbox)
  on the first attempt; do not try them in the workspace-write sandbox first.
- **Claude Code:** they need `"voyager resolve *"` in the sandbox's excluded
  commands. If a run returns `SANDBOX_BLOCKED`, ask the user to add
  `{"sandbox": {"excludedCommands": ["voyager resolve *"]}}` to their Claude Code
  settings, or to allow the command to run without the sandbox; do not retry it
  inside the sandbox.

Relay `SANDBOX_BLOCKED`'s remediation as given. It is
never an Accessibility problem: do not tell the user to change the Accessibility
permission, restart Resolve or reinstall Voyager over it.

Do not offer to operate Resolve's own controls. If the user explicitly asks you
to, `use-computer` is a manual attempt that has not been verified on Resolve: say
so.

Resolve Free has refused external scripting since 19.1, and 21.1 removed its
in-app Python too. Do not retry the Studio Python runner or install a Python bridge
to bypass that boundary.

Voyager runs its own in-app scripts in Resolve: the import, the edit and the inspection. Do not write other Lua
for Workspace > Scripts or press that menu yourself with AppleScript, osascript
or a shell clicker.

`resolve recipe free-import --write import.lua` is the same import as an in-app
recipe for a user who wants to run it by hand from Workspace > Scripts; prefer the
command.

# Resolve Studio

The user has DaVinci Resolve Studio. Start with `voyager resolve health --json`: it
checks the scripting connection Studio edits through. The CLI selects the official
Blackmagic MCP for supported installations and the compatible Python SDK backend
for older versions; use the same commands with either backend.

**Not set up** (`health` returns `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `INVALID_CONFIG` or
`VERSION_MISMATCH` with `scriptingReady: true`): scripting answers, but Voyager's
Resolve runtime is missing or stale, and workflow and script commands fail until it
is provisioned. Run `voyager resolve setup --json` yourself, then `health` again.
If setup returns `SERVICE_RUNNING`, finish active jobs, run `voyager resolve stop`,
then run setup again. This is not a Resolve preference; do not send the user to Preferences.

**Scripting unavailable** (`health` refuses, or a command returns
`SCRIPTING_UNAVAILABLE`): Voyager drives Studio through Resolve's external
scripting, which is off by default. If Resolve is not running, open it
(`open -a "DaVinci Resolve"`) and run `health` again. If it still refuses, ask the
user to open DaVinci Resolve > Preferences > System > General, set "External
scripting using" to Local, and click Save; then run `voyager resolve health --json`
again and continue once it connects. Relay any other remediation `health` gives,
such as finishing startup or closing a modal dialog. Do not repeatedly retry
unavailable scripting. If the user finds no "External scripting using" option, their
Resolve is the free edition: record it with `voyager resolve edition --set free`
and tell them Voyager uses [the free DaVinci Resolve workflow](free-resolve.md) from their next chat.

Prefer supported integration operations for precise edits; `use-computer` can fill
a missing UI control.

`voyager resolve workflow state --json` gives the current project,
timeline, version, edition, backend and render state.
If connection fails, use `resolve health` and follow its remediation; `resolve setup`
provisions the runtime these commands need when it is missing.
Name the project before edits, preserving the current project's contents:

```sh
voyager resolve project ensure --name "Intended project" --json
voyager resolve media import --files /absolute/source.mov /absolute/overlay.png --json
voyager resolve project save --json
```

`ensure` reuses the matching current project, names an unnamed project in place,
and only opens/creates the exact requested name when no project is open. A different
open project is a conflict, not permission to replace it. `project save --name NAME`
names and saves the current unnamed project (`Untitled Project`, or `Untitled Project
<date>_<time>` after Resolve relaunches from a crash) and answers Resolve's own
Save Current Project dialog if it is already open; no computer control is needed. Add `--project-id ID` when known. Imports reuse
exact paths already in the current media-pool folder.

## Write and execute

Read `voyager resolve docs scripts --json` for the execution contract.
Use `resolve recipe` to list adaptable examples; `resolve recipe assemble --write
edit.py` copies one to a new file.
For a new cut containing still images, `picture-cut` handles their exact durations;
native append can use the default still duration instead.
Look up unfamiliar methods with `resolve sdk TimelineItem.SetFades --json` or a
referenced type such as `resolve sdk FadeInfo --json`. `resolve sdk --search "audio|volume"`
searches installed API descriptions; `--api fusion` selects Fusion.

```sh
voyager resolve script run --file edit.py --input @edit-plan.json \
  --project-id PROJECT_ID --timeline-id TIMELINE_ID --json
```

Scripts receive `resolve`, `project_manager`, `project`, `timeline`, `params`, and
`workdir` (the caller's directory). Return plain data through `result`. Resolve
asset paths against `workdir`; the service does not change its process directory.
Target flags check identity; they do not select a project or timeline.

For an image in a Fusion comp, use `loader = add_fusion_loader(comp, "assets/image.png")`:
it checks the file relative to `workdir`, suppresses the picker, sets and verifies
the Clip path, and returns the native node. For other Loader/Saver creation, use
`add_fusion_tool(comp, "Loader")` or `"Saver"`, then set an absolute path.
The runner guards ordinary `comp.AddTool(...)`
too, locking only creation to suppress automatic file pickers. Avoid shorthand
constructors or reflective/imported creation that bypasses this guard. Keep
parameter writes outside composition locks so the changes render correctly.
A Fusion **Loader** file picker asks for media, not a project: do not respond by loading another project
or restarting Resolve. Inspect and resolve that specific dialog,
then continue from the existing composition.

### Preview without render dialogs

For Fusion titles, check the exact font **family and style in the running Fusion font
list** (the Text+ controls or a supported API found through `resolve sdk --api
fusion --search FontManager`), and prove one composition before repeating it. A `.ttf`
in the project folder is only an asset;
TextPlus `Font`/`Style` expect registered names, not that file's path or filename.
Do not assume installing it refreshes a running editor.

For a timeline-frame proof, set and read back the intended timeline timecode, then
use `project.ExportCurrentFrameAsStill(absolute_image_path)`. It can return True
and still write an all-black PNG. For a moving preview, render the timeline and extract
review frames from that file.

If an expected picture is black, stop bulk title writes and full export. On macOS,
`~/Library/Application Support/Blackmagic Design/DaVinci Resolve/logs/ResolveDebug.txt`
can report `Could not find font`, followed by Merge foreground and MediaOut input
failures. Edit the existing nodes instead of adding another composition.
Do not use a full render or
cycling presets to diagnose already-black proofs.

Do not use Fusion `comp.Render(...)` for unattended proofs. It can open a
"Render completed!" modal even with `Wait=True`, guessed `Flags`, or
`Fusion().NewComp(True, False, True)`. Rewrite the proof using the timeline routes; do not
bypass the guard through imported code or reflective calls. A completion popup
does not mean the render failed: inspect the output before rendering again.

For a useful individual action, `resolve describe TOOL --action ACTION` supplies
its contract and `resolve call TOOL --action ACTION --input @params.json` executes
it.
For resumable sequences, read `resolve docs agent-workflows` and use workflow batches.

## Recovery and delivery

A CLI wait timeout leaves the operation pending. Use `resolve doctor --json` for independent
dialog/permission diagnostics and collect the same `op_…` with `resolve job wait ID`.
Matched supported dialogs can recover using the original operation's supplied intent;
unknown/ambiguous dialogs remain blocked. Do not enqueue SDK probes behind a
blocked operation. If Resolve exited, reopen saved work with `resolve project open --name "Exact name"`
(existing projects only; preserves outgoing work), then inspect workflow state.
Never automatically replay edits, even after switching backends; a script failure may
leave partial edits, so inspect its output and editor state before resuming.
Official script execution is capped at 60 seconds; use bounded batches and the render command for long renders. A native execution timeout has an unknown outcome, not a pending receipt that guarantees continued execution. Native render IDs
are separate from CLI operation IDs.

If computer control reports `not_dispatched` / `DriverError.Tool`, no UI action happened. Stop
retrying that driver, retain the operation ID and diagnose its failure; a ready
status alone does not prove window inspection or input works. Do not replace this
with guessed clicks, repeated permission requests, or another editor restart.

A window saying `Problem Report for DaVinci Resolve` and `DaVinci Resolve quit
unexpectedly` is a crash reporter, even if its process is named `Resolve`. It is
not a save dialog or evidence that the original editor is still rendering. Voyager
records `editorExit: crash_reporter` (or `process_identity_changed` for a replaced
editor) and preserves the original operation's uncertain outcome. Collect that
operation until terminal before submitting more work. Do not send the crash report.
Keep the receipt, match the timestamp in `crash_archive.txt` / `ResolveDebug.txt`, and reopen the intended saved project.

`VERSION_MISMATCH` means CLI/service code differs, not that the project is corrupt: finish active jobs,
stop the broker with `resolve stop`, provision with `resolve setup`, then reread
state. This does not require restarting Resolve.

For normal delivery, use the owned render command instead of writing a render
script or cycling presets:

```sh
voyager resolve render start --path exports/final.mp4 \
  --project-id PROJECT --timeline-id TIMELINE --json
voyager resolve render-wait JOB --project-id PROJECT --timeout 120 --json
```

`render start` and `render recover` make `--timeline-id` the current timeline when it
is in the open project; other commands only check it. `.mp4` selects H.264; `.mov` selects ProRes 422 HQ. This preserves timeline size,
frame rate and full range, initializes Deliver state, pins an available base preset,
checks native settings, and records the job before starting. `render inspect --json` reads installed options; use advanced
`call render` actions for other formats. `recipe deliver` separately packages the
DRP/media and returns the render command. Never clear the whole render queue to clean up a probe.

If a response has `ok:false`, read its top-level `error` and receipt before extracting
`data`; filtering only `data` hides the cause. Reuse the original operation/job ID
and destination receipt after uncertainty. Use `resolve render recover --path ORIGINAL --project-id PROJECT --timeline-id TIMELINE`
to reconcile the receipt with the queue/output. It does not resubmit by default. If
both are absent, `--retry-missing` explicitly authorizes another attempt and preserves
the old receipt; absence now does not prove the previous attempt never ran.

If Resolve quits while a render is being queued, Voyager returns
`RESOLVE_CRASHED_DURING_RENDER_SUBMISSION`. A receipt stopped at
`lastStage: submitting` without `job_id` marks the same boundary: `AddRenderJob`,
before `StartRendering`. Resolve Studio 21.1 (0.14 and 0.0017) has aborted there with
`LoadTimelineFilterToRecord` / `GetUseProjectTimelineFilter()` on script-built
timelines even after Voyager initialized Deliver. On a customer install that hit
it, Quick Export (`RenderWithQuickExport`) crashed Resolve too.

After Resolve has exited, reopen the project and verify the intended timeline and
healthy session (`render start` saves just before submission; Quick Export does not).
Reconcile the original queue/output with `render recover --path ORIGINAL` before
retrying. Reuse an existing job or verify an existing output rather than duplicate it.
If no matching job/output exists and no render is active, **proceed with one native
Resolve retry under the existing export authorization**: use the same destination
with `render recover --path ORIGINAL --retry-missing`. Without a receipt, inspect the
queue/output explicitly, then use `render start`. A first crash does not require
fresh permission or proving the root cause. Recovery alone is not an export attempt;
report whether a retry actually ran.

A supported alternative preset, Quick Export or the Deliver page can be that retry
if it fits the requested deliverable; these share Resolve's renderer and are not
proven crash workarounds. If the same failure recurs, stop cycling equivalent routes
and diagnose from the receipts/logs before another render. Keep Resolve as the
requested renderer. Do not substitute an FFmpeg reconstruction
without the user's agreement.

`RENDER_STUCK` (and `render.stuck: true` in `resolve state`) means Resolve reports a
render in progress while every queued job is complete, failed or cancelled. In that
state Resolve has refused saves, edits and new renders, and `StopRendering` has not
cleared it. Do not keep stopping, queuing or preparing renders: if it persists, ask
the user to quit and reopen Resolve. If a render call stops responding, inspect
`resolve job list` (`NATIVE_CALL_PENDING`) instead of issuing more Resolve calls behind it.

For Quick Export, inspect
`resolve call render --action quick_export_capabilities --json` and then
`resolve describe render --action safe_quick_export --json`. Use an advertised
preset appropriate to the requested deliverable, a new empty output directory,
and `allow_render: true` (`require_temp_target: false` for a delivery directory).
This action forces uploads off. Collect the same operation ID if the CLI wait
expires.

For editable handoff, prefer `resolve recipe deliver` (DRP plus copied media and
relink mapping). A separate `ArchiveProject` call crashed in the same 21.1 build;
do not add a raw `.dra` archive as a recovery step or repeat it after a crash.

For gain, fades and mixing, read `resolve docs finishing` before concluding the SDK
cannot adjust audio.

For transparent overlays or black backgrounds, see [transparency](transparency.md).

Read only what the edit needs:

- `resolve docs scripting-recipes`: timing, replacement, titles and delivery routes.
- `resolve docs editorial-decision-guide`: shot selection and pacing.
- `resolve docs finishing`: sound, color and final review.
- `resolve docs color-decision-guide`: deeper color decisions and capability limits.

# Transparent overlays

For Remotion overlays, use this direct export first (all four settings matter):

```sh
voyager remotion run ./<piece>/motion -- render src/index.tsx Overlay out/overlay.mov \
  --codec=prores --prores-profile=4444 --pixel-format=yuva444p10le --image-format=png
```

The composition itself must have a transparent background.

In Resolve, use `media_pool_item` → `set_clip_property` with the imported `clip_id`,
`key: "Alpha mode"`, and `value: "Straight"` or `"Premultiplied"` according to the
source; use `Straight` for the direct Remotion export above. Inspect `actual` and `verified` in the response. For direct scripts, read
`GetClipProperty("Alpha mode")` after `SetClipProperty(...)`.

Export to a fresh filename and import that file; do not keep testing an older
media-pool reference after replacing a render.

If valid file alpha still renders opaque after verified import settings, use a
**PNG image sequence** on a separate Resolve video track. This preserved editable
layers in a reproduced ProRes-alpha failure; do not flatten the footage as the
first fallback.

Import the sequence as **one clip**, with the actual first/last frame numbers:

```python
clips = project.GetMediaPool().ImportMedia([{
    "FilePath": "/absolute/out/overlay-frames/frame_%06d.png",
    "StartIndex": 1, "EndIndex": frame_count,
}])
```

Match the imported clip FPS to the composition before placement; keep the frame
folder with the project.

## Which edition

The environment block names the detected edition: "DaVinci Resolve Studio" or
"DaVinci Resolve (free)". Follow the matching workflow:

- DaVinci Resolve Studio, the paid edition: [Studio](references/studio-resolve.md).
- The free DaVinci Resolve: [Free](references/free-resolve.md).

When the edition is unknown, settle it before acting on Resolve:

1. Run `voyager resolve edition --check --json`. It reads the edition inside an
   open Resolve and records it.
2. If it still returns `unknown`, ask the user with your question tool, once:
   "Which DaVinci Resolve do you have?" with the options "DaVinci Resolve (Free)"
   and "DaVinci Resolve Studio". Record the answer with
   `voyager resolve edition --set free` or `--set studio`. Never ask when the
   edition is already known.
3. Follow the matching workflow.

## Review footage locally before choosing edits

When selecting takes, dialogue lines or cut points, reuse existing evidence or run
`voyager speech transcribe FILE --local --output DIR` for word timings without
speaker labels, and `voyager media review FILE --json` for loudness, silence and
picture checks. Both process footage on this computer without uploading it, in
either Resolve edition. Follow [local footage review](../edit-video/SKILL.md#review-footage-locally)
for interpreting the evidence and its limits.
To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [hosted media understanding](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).

## Both editions

**Windows:** Studio works through the same scripting commands as on macOS; there
`edition --check` reads the edition through that connection, so Resolve must be open
with "External scripting using" set to Local. Free 19.1 and later on Windows is
recognised from Resolve.exe itself. Free there has no scripting connection, and `free-import` and `free-edit` run only on macOS: write the cut with
`voyager resolve timeline write` and have the user import it with File > Import >
Timeline.

**Mac App Store Resolve:** it is sandboxed and runs no scripts, so Voyager cannot
work in it (`RESOLVE_APP_STORE_UNSUPPORTED`). Relay the remediation: install Resolve
from blackmagicdesign.com; the free download works.

One chat drives Resolve at a time. A command that changes Resolve waits up to 15 s while
another chat holds it; `RESOURCE_BUSY` names that chat. Then do other work or end your
turn; do not retry in a loop. For several edits that must not interleave with another
chat, add `--hold` to keep Resolve until your turn ends, or release it sooner with
`voyager resolve release`.

Never quit, kill (`kill`, `killall`, `pkill`) or restart a running DaVinci Resolve; it
holds the user's projects. If it seems stuck, ask the user to save and restart it.

Source and timeline frame rates may differ and a timeline can start at 01:00:00:00;
check actual bounds. To change one title or shot, revise it or a named variant and keep
the surrounding edit; don't rebuild a finished timeline.
